analysis:
The supplied change is CHANGELOG.md only: it adds an 'Unreleased - machine-scoped Autopilot' section (patch hunk @@ -1,4 +1,11 @@, new lines 3-9). No source code, tests, auth paths or config are included, so only the documentation is reviewable. The entry describes behavior that touches threat-model areas, but those implementations are not in this batch:
- Persisted per-machine desired Autopilot mode, defaulting to shadow, edited via authenticated admin endpoints (TB-006, T-024).
- Live control requires verified identity, provider consent and acknowledgement. Global shadow and pause override machine intent. Mode revisions revoke stale grants, and failed policy reads remove live authority (TB-002, TB-011, T-053).
- Capacity-freshness checks are kept current across policy reads and durable command delivery.
- Lease enqueue avoids waiting on a concurrent socket close while registry/provider locks are held. Shutdown still stops admission before draining queued frames, and in-flight cancellation waits for the transport fence (TB-002 availability).
The changelog states the change does not deploy or activate a production cohort. It makes no claim that weakens the serving-authorization, App Attest or legacy MDM trust model, and it does not invalidate any stated threat assumption. Next-pass reviewers should check the actual code for four things: (1) the admin endpoints enforce admin-key authorization and audit logging; (2) live Autopilot commands are rechecked at final dispatch (authorizeInferenceHandoff-style) and fail closed on policy-read errors; (3) the lock-ordering change does not open a race between close and enqueue; (4) the threat model may need an update for the new admin surface and the Autopilot control boundary if they ship. Coverage limit: the implementation is not supplied, so no code-level safety conclusion can be drawn.
